rubrics.criterion: Running the same structural rule that fires on the starting state over the repaired tree reports no function signature: no signature in the workspace still receives as loose, individually named parameters a group of three or more values that another signature in the same crate receives under the same names.
rubrics.rationale: The starting state carries the recurring-parameter-group relation at exactly four signatures in two crates; a repair that leaves any one of them threaded member-by-member has localized but not resolved the case.

rubrics.criterion: The CLI output options threaded in the starting state (the validate gate and the inline/raw-string/sort-keys rendering flags) reach process_json and format_json behind one owner that carries them as a unit — an existing record they already belong to or a fitting new one — at both signatures.
rubrics.rationale: This is the cluster in the binary crate; the outcome is the unit being carried, not any particular owner type, so a solver reusing the parsed-arguments record and one introducing a dedicated options record both satisfy it.

rubrics.criterion: The tape-build context threaded in the starting state (the scratch buffers, the token slice, the input document) is held by or with the evaluator that owns the buffers, so both build paths that were free helper functions reach the context through one owner rather than receiving it member-by-member.
rubrics.rationale: The second cluster lives in the runner's lazy evaluator; the buffers and the input already have a natural owner, and the borrowed scratch copy of the escaped branch must stay distinguishable from the pristine input.

rubrics.criterion: No participating signature or call site merely repacks the recurring group into a pass-through container whose members are immediately spelled back out as the same loose variables at each stop (a raw tuple or a record with the identical field names destructured at every caller).
rubrics.rationale: A rename hop is the degenerate 'repair' for this case: the clump would survive with new syntax, so the criterion rejects it regardless of which container type a solver picks.

rubrics.criterion: Every call site that restated the recurring members in the starting state — the three CLI input paths in main and the two unit tests for the option flags, plus the callers of the tape-build helpers — passes the owning abstraction instead, leaving no spelling-out of the member list anywhere.
rubrics.rationale: The threading in the starting state is duplicated at five CLI call points and at the tape-build dispatch; a repair that migrates only the signatures and not the edges leaves half the repetition, which is what future option additions would trip over.

rubrics.criterion: The wiring around the two build paths survives identically through the regrouping: the escaped-input scan still selects between them, the declined outcome still records document starts from the pristine input, and the divergence gate still compares against the pristine input rather than against mutated scratch bytes.
rubrics.rationale: The clump in the runner sits directly on the fallback contract that keeps two evaluators in byte parity; the regrouping must carry the pristine-versus-scratch distinction, not smooth it away.

rubrics.criterion: Any new owner type introduced for the tape-build context is defined once, beside the evaluator in the runner crate, and the binary crate grows no parallel copy of it.
rubrics.rationale: The context belongs to a runner-internal responsibility; a second definition in the binary crate would be the same clump wearing a second coat and would quietly fork the fallback types.

rubrics.criterion: Nothing the regrouping made unnecessary survives: helpers that existed only to receive the threaded members, record fields or methods that no longer have readers, and imports the removals orphaned are all gone rather than left unwired.
rubrics.rationale: The starting state exists precisely because an extraction was left half-finished; leaving the extraneous halves wired-or-idle after the repair would hand the same aftertaste to the next maintainer.

rubrics.criterion: The repaired tree does not keep two coexisting ways to pass the same group — the owning abstraction alongside a still-reachable loose-parameter path (for example a retained parameter-list variant that some caller still uses).
rubrics.rationale: Two live routes for one piece of data is the most plausible short-cut failure here: it keeps the spread alive while adding a third shape to maintain.

rubrics.criterion: The zero-copy property of the unescaped tape build survives the regrouping: the input document the CLI holds is still mutated in place with no fresh per-document copy introduced to make one owner type fit both branches.
rubrics.rationale: Both branches carry the input under different borrows in the starting state; making the owner uniform by always copying would change the performance-defining behavior the lazy path exists for, without changing any test result.

rubrics.criterion: The repair changes neither which inputs the tape path serves nor which it declines to the Value-based evaluator, and touches no signature inside the frozen Value-based evaluator (runner.rs, array.rs, object.rs).
rubrics.rationale: Silently widening the decline set routes more inputs through the slower evaluator without any test noticing; the frozen evaluator is the public oracle face of the runner and out of bounds by repository policy.

rubrics.criterion: The new owner does not over-collect: single-consumer data that travels with the group in the starting state (the validate-only gate, the query text) is not folded into the rendering-option record nor into the tape-context owner, forcing data no reader uses onto every stop.
rubrics.rationale: Over-bundling is the failure mode a solver reaches for when one record is easier than two owners; it recreates the fat-parameter smell the repository removed the Args record from the internals to avoid.
